title: Runtime Cohesion and Integration Manual
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview
--------
This manual describes how the serving runtime components must integrate to preserve predictable inference SLAs while enabling safe experimentation. It consolidates architecture contracts, scheduler integration expectations, a compact profiling playbook, benchmarking guidance, release checklists, and concise runbook actions. The audience is runtime engineers, platform owners, and SREs who operate or extend the inference stack.

Scope
-----
Covers the following subsystems and artifacts: inference-router, kernel-coordinator, kernel-manager, kv-cache, fidelity-orchestrator, batching-service, telemetry-adapter, and the benchmarking harness (op-sim). It intentionally excludes SDK-level API ergonomics and customer Console UI.

Design principles
-----------------
- Observable contracts: every handoff between components must carry an event with correlation_id and causality_trace.
- Fail-fast, degrade-safe: fallbacks must preserve API success (200s) with explicit fidelity headers when possible.
- Testability: each integration point must be exercised via the op-sim harness before rollout.
- Bounded blast radius: experimental scheduler plugins run in sandbox cohorts with quota-limited traffic.

Architecture components and responsibilities
------------------------------------------
- inference-router: performs tenant routing, request classification, and initial priority tagging. Must attach request.metadata.priority and request.metadata.expiry_ts.
- kernel-coordinator: authoritative placement decision-maker; returns allocation tokens and kernel_hint (e.g., "segmented-attn-v2", "quantized-8bit").
- kernel-manager: asserts kernel version compatibility, triggers handoff to the GPU dispatcher, and surfaces kernel telemetry with kernel_signature and kernel_commit.
- kv-cache: manages prefix caches per-session; emits cache_warmup events and provides warmup_score (0..1).
- fidelity-orchestrator: maps workload -> model_variant with policy evaluation (latency vs cost vs quality).
- batching-service: consolidates requests, exposes queue_depth and current_burst_size metrics.
- telemetry-adapter: normalises and annotates traces for downstream SLO dashboards.

Scheduler integration contract (must be implemented on every kernel path)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Table: Required fields on kernel allocation response
| field | type | meaning | example |
| correlation_id | string | mirrors router trace | rtr-01b2.. |
| allocation_token | string | ephemeral token to acquire GPU slot | tok-3ef4.. |
| kernel_hint | string | suggested kernel variant | segmented-attn-v2 |
| estimated_tail_ms | int | estimated tail latency for this request shape | 45 |
| fallback_variants | list | ordered fallbacks when capacity misses | [lrg-8q, lrg-4q] |

Behavioral expectations:
1) kernel-manager must validate allocation_token within 200ms of issuance.
2) If kernel-manager cannot satisfy kernel_hint, it must return first compatible fallback_variants and set response.header.x-fidelity-degraded = true.
3) Any allocation that waits > 2s must be annotated with queue_backpressure=true and emit an alert to the SLO monitoring stream.

Profiling playbook (compact)
---------------------------
Purpose: enable fast root cause between request-shape, kernel choice, KV hit-rate, and tail-latency.
Quick steps:
1) Reproduce under op-sim with identical request distribution (seeded corpus).
2) Enable full trace on a 1% sampleset (trace_level=full) for 10 minutes.
3) Correlate kernel_signature -> kernel_latency_ms histogram and kv_hit boolean.
4) If tail > SLO (95p > 120ms), run microbench: single-tenant kernel warmstart and memory-pressure sweep.
Useful commands:
- ./op-sim run --profile-corpus corpuses/production-seed-2026.json --sampling 1%
- curl -H "X-Debug-Trace: capture" https://inference-router/api/v1/debug/trace?request_id=<id>

Benchmarking suite guidance
--------------------------
- Baselines: maintain L1 baselines for the following canonical shapes: short-chat (<=64 tokens), long-completion (>=512 tokens), embedding-batch (batch_size=128).
- Metrics to capture: p50, p90, p95 token latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, CPU steal, KV hit-rate, and per-token cost_estimate_usd.
- Canary policy: new kernel builds must pass the op-sim synthetic corpus with <=+5% p95 regression and <=+2% cost increase versus baseline.
- Repro steps for suspect builds: 1) pin commit, 2) run three independent op-sim runs at scaled load (0.25x, 0.75x, 1.25x), 3) run kernel microbenchmark with isolated device.

Release and rollout checklist (runtime component)
------------------------------------------------
1) Feature branch: include integration tests that validate allocation_token flow.
2) Pre-merge: create a canary matrix (tenants, shapes, model-variants) and run op-sim.
3) Canary: deploy to 5% traffic in region-us-west1 for 24 hours. Monitor: p95 latency, error-rate, kernel-failure-rate.
4) Gradual roll: 25% -> 60% -> 100% with 1h gates and automated rollback on SLO breach.
5) Post-mortem: collect trace samples and a kernel-perf snapshot.

Known issues and mitigations
--------------------------
- Symptom: sporadic 500s on long-completion shapes when KV cache warmup_score is low.
  Mitigation: enable prefetch for sessions with entropy_score < 0.15 and increase kv-cache prewarm concurrency.
- Symptom: kernel-manager reports transient kernel_commit mismatch after rolling kernel update.
  Mitigation: adopt dual-run intersection checks: kernels serve concurrently for 30 minutes while allocation_token includes kernel_commit_v2.
- Symptom: burst-traffic leads to request prioritisation inversion.
  Mitigation: enforce priority drain windows and apply reserve slots for high-SLA tenants (reserve ratio 0.12).

Runbook (quick actions)
----------------------
1) P95 latency spike (owner: runtime-oncall):
   a) check telemetry-adapter for sudden drop in kv_hit_rate and burst in queue_depth.
   b) if kernel failures > 0.5% in last 10m, flip canary fallback routing (set routing.policy.fallback_rate=0.4).
   c) scale up dedicated burst-pool by +20% for 15 minutes.
2) Kernel deadlock (owner: kernel-team):
   a) identify affected host via kernel-heartbeat missing.
   b) set host to drain and restart kernel-manager process with core-dump enabled.
   c) redirect traffic via inference-router override to alternate pool.

Ownership, escalation and docs
-----------------------------
- Primary owner: Runtime Platform team (runtime-platform@redwood.ai).
- Oncall rotation: runtime-oncall (pager duty) handled by eng-sre and runtime engineers.
- Escalation matrix: runtime-oncall -> kernel-team lead -> eng-sre manager -> CPE.

Appendix: sample config snippets
-------------------------------
1) kernel-allocation response (JSON example):
{
  "correlation_id": "rtr-01b2abcd",
  "allocation_token": "tok-3ef4xyz",
  "kernel_hint": "segmented-attn-v2",
  "estimated_tail_ms": "45",
  "fallback_variants": "[lrg-8q,lrg-4q]"
}

2) op-sim command to run canary corpus:
./op-sim run --corpus corpuses/canary-may-2026.json --concurrency 64 --capture-traces yes --output results/canary-may-2026.json
